summary.headline: HFL posted record FY26 PAT of INR149 crores (+29% YoY) and guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, while cash flow lagged on working capital.
summary.overview: Hindustan Foods delivered record FY26 profitability: total income rose 17% to INR4,264 crores, EBITDA 20% to INR377 crores, and PAT 29% to INR149 crores. Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR104 crores (+28%), and PAT INR41.5 crores (+32%). Footwear was hit hardest by petrochemical and freight inflation in Q4 and expected to remain affected in Q1 FY27, while pass-through in other verticals continues. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores but moved the GST inversion-driven shift from gross to net revenue recognition to Q2-Q3 FY27, and withheld sales and segment profitability guidance.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Sales expected at roughly INR500 crores in FY26 and INR700-800 crores in FY27 per management. Broke even in Q2 FY26 and said it is PAT positive, but Q4 margins were hit as polymer prices rose ~50-60% and freight rose; pass-through to customers is delayed and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in Q4 aided by season and new capacity. Panipat plant commissioned April 2026 (capacity ~20,000 tons vs ~35,000-40,000 tons made in FY26). Cone facility acquired and stick facility commissioned; INR50 crore brownfield expansion planned at Lucknow and Panipat.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in the season. New bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27; targets becoming largest independent bottler in India by end FY27, operating as shared manufacturing. INR50 crore investment signed for FY27.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care
segments.commentary: Steady momentum in FY26. Aurangabad personal care facility integrated from 1 April 2026. Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27. INR50 crore HPC investment signed for FY27. Management cites strong engagement in home care.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Added customers and completed several domestic and international audits; signed 3-4 new customers for the inherited facility (Baddi, acquired from Reckitt, ~INR220 crore difference between paid and book value). Establishing dedicated ayurvedic wellness facility at Baddi. No revenue or profit figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores reiterated; management did not give sales guidance.
Target of 20% EBITDA growth and 20% ROE mandated for each of the five verticals.
Planned FY27 capex of about INR2,150 crores (gross block) with a 60:40 dedicated-to-shared split; INR150 crores of new contracts signed since April 2026.
Gross-to-net revenue recognition shift for some food businesses moved from Q1-Q2 to Q2-Q3 FY27; management says no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT, but margins will look better.
Footwear profitability not guided; customer price pass-through expected to be concluded within about a month.
Management says EBITDA margin of 10% is achievable; PAT margin of 10% unlikely on a like-to-like basis.
capex_capacity: Gross block including CWIP and advances reached INR1,800 crores at March 2026; FY26 capex was above INR700 crores, with a gap of about INR190 crores against the earlier INR2,000 crore-odd gross block target.
Panipat ice cream plant commissioned April 2026 in under 10 months; about INR200 crores invested, earnings start FY27.
Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27; new beverage bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27.
Baddi ayurvedic wellness facility under establishment, alongside modernisation at the existing Baddi facility; footwear capacity expansion across North and South India.
Management says underutilised assets of about INR508 crores are ramping up; ROCE threshold for new projects is about 18% IRR.
demand_pricing: Footwear polymer prices up roughly 50-60% and freight up; footwear is the only division where raw material pass-through is not immediate. Customers are reportedly supportive.
Most other businesses pass through raw material and packaging cost increases immediately.
Management sees strong customer engagement in home care, beverages and ice cream; export push for healthcare planned, with US modern trade talks under way.
Gross-to-net shift stems from GST inverted duty structure from September 2025: food inputs such as packaging attract higher GST than the 5% on finished foods.
Management declined to name customers, including Reliance's ice cream entry.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear FY26 sales and profitability, and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales reached about INR500 crores in FY26 and expects INR700-800 crores in FY27. It declined to give a profitability target, citing raw material volatility and ongoing customer talks. CFO said the division broke even in Q2 and is now PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block split between dedicated and shared facilities after completing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Samdani said the split is about 61% dedicated and 39% shared currently and will stay in a similar range on INR2,150 crores of planned gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment moves to net revenue model and what is the impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said this is mainly food, where packaging and some raw materials carry higher GST. The timeline slipped to Q2-Q3 FY27. Bottom-line EBITDA and PAT are unaffected, but margins will look better as sales fall.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pressure in footwear not hit FY27 PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification across categories should offset footwear headwinds through more than compensatory growth elsewhere. It remains confident in the PAT guidance but cannot yet see how long the uncertainty will last.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise profitability and shared versus dedicated ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined segment EBITDA, promising disclosure by year end, and shared that the gross block by segment is in the presentation. Shared manufacturing targets higher ROCE than dedicated. Dedicated ROE targets are 16-22% pre-tax. Footwear is 100% shared.

qa_highlights.question: Financing of incremental capex given working capital pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said working capital credit has been secured across product lines and is not constraining capex. Net debt to equity is 0.84x with cash buffer, but management will be more cautious and not go all out on investments.

risks_watch: Footwear margin pressure from polymer and freight costs, with pass-through to customers not yet concluded and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.
Gross-to-net revenue shift (Q2-Q3 FY27) will reduce reported sales; customer agreement count was not disclosed and must be confirmed next call.
Working capital and inventory build pressured cash flow; cash flow was described as less than satisfactory.

Reconciliation gaps: net capital employed uses two-year average equity and net debt less cash; Baddi acquisition creates a roughly INR220 crore difference in gross block; investor query on reconciliation was deferred offline.
Only INR150 crores of new contracts signed since April 2026; FY27 capex achievement against INR2,150 crores depends on further announcements.
LPG shortage temporarily affected two factories.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY27 PAT guidance and the long-term 20% growth mandate, but cautious on footwear, sales guidance, cash flow and capex pace. Management was defensive on the reconciliation of capital employed and ROCE figures and deflected some questions to later calls.
key_quotes: So we should be about INR700 crores to INR800 crores of turnover as far as shoes is concerned in this FY27.

We will stick to the guidance of the PAT, which for next year, we've given a very clear guidance even last quarter, and we've reiterated it in this quarter, which is we are confident that we should be able to get to a PAT of between INR200 crores to INR220 crores for FY27.
this will not affect our bottom line numbers, whether it is of EBITDA or whether it is of the PAT in absolute way.
